summary: Round r1 (restricted network; data hosts blocked; shared WebSearch budget exhausted except one query). All three questions are answered only at the level of research design; every empirical item is pending. Q1 (peg transmission of Indian inflation and INR/USD): leads are NRB CPI tables in the CME releases (FY2024/25 annual, FY2025/26 nine/ten-month, August 2026), NRB forex page/API and historical exchange-rate workbooks, NRB research on Indian monetary spillovers, RBI DBIE, reference-rate archive, Handbook and the June/August 2026 MPC documents, and IMF WEO for India CPI. Q2 (months of import cover and its volatility): NRB CME monthly reserve and import-cover tables (archive plus annual tables back to FY2019/20 and earlier), the IMF 2026 Article IV/seventh ECF review staff report (reserve adequacy), WDI FI.RES.TOTL.MO as a calendar-year cross-check. Q3 (implication for NPR/USD in the GDP model): recorded as an identity-based constraint (NPR/USD = peg ratio x INR/USD while the peg holds) consistent with 20B; INR/USD is the exogenous driver and the peg ratio a parameter with a break-scenario. No numbers are reported; the peg ratio itself is to be read from the NRB forex page.

findings.claim: Q3 (identity): while the NPR-INR peg holds, NPR/USD equals the fixed NPR/INR ratio times INR/USD, up to rate-type and averaging differences; NPR/USD should therefore not be projected independently in the GDP model. INR/USD is the exogenous driver; the peg ratio is a parameter.
findings.note: Consistent with 20B challenge to 03. Empirical verification of the identity is pending (INR/USD and NPR/USD series).

findings.claim: Q3: For scenario work, a long-run NPR/USD path is constructed only as INR/USD path assumption x peg ratio; a separate peg-adjustment (re-peg/devaluation) stress case is modelled as a discrete step, not as a trend. Neither is a forecast.

Q3: Nominal USD GDP growth under the peg equals NPR nominal growth minus INR/USD depreciation (approximately); a real appreciation from Nepal-India inflation differentials does not change the nominal NPR/USD path but affects competitiveness (REER) and the tradables sector.
findings.note: Trade-off to report to 01/15: a USD GDP target cannot be helped by the exchange rate under the peg, while real appreciation from remittance inflows may weaken tradables.

findings.claim: Q1 (hypothesis): Indian inflation transmits to Nepal mainly through the price of India-sourced imports (majority of trade with India, INR-settled) and the open border, while INR/USD movements transmit through third-country import prices and USD-denominated remittance receipts; to be tested.

data_gaps: No NRB, RBI, IMF or WB file was downloaded in r1 (hosts blocked); every series awaits `python -m src.cli leads --fetch` and ingestion in r2.
NRB Monetary Policy FY2026/27 (2083/84) document (inflation ceiling and reserve-adequacy target) not located as a direct file.

A single machine-readable monthly NRB file for reserves, import cover and CPI back to FY2010/11 not located; series must be assembled from CME monthly releases or NRB Quarterly Economic Bulletin tables.
Currency composition of reserves (INR vs convertible) and the definition of the import base in NRB's import-cover ratio need confirmation from table notes.
No located study estimates INR/USD-to-Nepal CPI pass-through directly; an original estimate (labelled estimate with method) may be needed in r2.
Several leads are from general knowledge (WDI FI.RES.TOTL.MO, IMF ARA) and are marked unverified.

assumptions.text: The NPR-INR peg is maintained over the model horizon in the baseline; a peg-adjustment case is a scenario stress, not a forecast.

Monthly Indian and US-dollar series are re-aggregated to Nepal FY (mid-July to mid-July) by day-weighting; mid-month Nepali-calendar boundaries approximated by Gregorian mid-month (same convention as 20A-A1).
NRB reference middle rate (average of buying and selling) is used for NPR/USD model inputs unless 00B/01C registers a different convention (C-18).
Import cover is computed on goods-and-services imports as the primary metric and merchandise-only as secondary, matching NRB presentation; to be confirmed on retrieval.

challenges.text: Any long-run NPR/USD path in the GDP/target arithmetic must be derived from an INR/USD assumption times the peg ratio (not an independent NPR depreciation trend); report the USD-GDP sensitivity to INR/USD explicitly.
Add a watch item for reserve import cover: NRB (FY, own import base) vs IMF staff report (possibly prospective imports) vs WDI FI.RES.TOTL.MO (CY, incl. gold). Likely definitional; keep all values.
Agree on one rate type (middle vs selling) and averaging (FY average vs end-period) for NPR/USD and INR/USD before 03A tests the peg identity; please share the convention adopted.
Accepted: interbank rates will be modelled on domestic liquidity first (remittance inflows, government balances), with RBI/Fed rates as a secondary exogenous channel.

uncertainty: High. No value retrieved. The transmission mechanism and pass-through are hypotheses; reserve-cover volatility cannot be characterised until monthly NRB series are assembled. Definitions of import cover differ across NRB, IMF and WDI; CPI basket rebasing and FY/CY mismatch add measurement uncertainty. Peg-continuity is a baseline assumption and its failure would dominate every NPR/USD result.

peg_transmission_notes.question: How does the NPR-INR peg transmit Indian inflation and INR/USD movements to Nepal?
peg_transmission_notes.method: (1) Verify identity NPR/USD = peg ratio x INR/USD on daily NRB and RBI/FBIL data and measure residual spreads; (2) distributed-lag regression of Nepal monthly CPI inflation (headline, food, non-food) on India CPI inflation and on change in INR/USD, FY2010/11 onward, with food/fuel price controls and structural-break tests; (3) compare with NRB research on Indian monetary spillovers; (4) qualitative channel map: INR-settled India trade, open border, third-country imports priced in USD, remittances in USD/GCC currencies.
known_issues: INR-settled vs convertible-currency settlement of India trade

reserve_cover_series.question: How many months of imports do gross reserves cover, and how volatile is that cover?
reserve_cover_series.method: Record NRB-published import cover monthly (observation); recompute as gross reserves / trailing 12-month goods-and-services imports x 12 (estimate) to check consistency; compute volatility (std. dev., range, maximum drawdown and episode dating) over FY2010/11-latest; compare with IMF staff report and WDI FI.RES.TOTL.MO noting definitional differences; decompose changes into current-account, capital/financial-account and valuation components using BoP tables.
reserve_cover_series.benchmarks: Conventional import-cover and ARA metrics to be cited from IMF ARA methodology on retrieval; no threshold asserted in r1.

fx_assumption_constraints.question: What does the peg imply for any long-run NPR/USD assumption in the GDP model?
constraints: NPR/USD is derived: peg ratio x INR/USD; never an independent trend while the peg holds (03A-A1).
INR/USD path is an exogenous scenario input supplied with source (RBI/FBIL history for calibration; 20B for long-run history).
Peg adjustment is a discrete scenario shock with explicit reserve and inflation consequences, not a smooth trend.
USD nominal GDP = NPR nominal GDP / (peg ratio x INR/USD); growth, deflator and exchange-rate effects kept separate (CLAUDE.md rule 6).
Rate type and FY averaging follow the convention registered by 00B/01C (C-02, C-18).
fx_assumption_constraints.method: Back-test the identity on FY averages; quantify historical INR/USD depreciation distribution (Indian FY) from RBI Handbook to bound scenario ranges; document in config/model_config.yaml via Agent 01 (not edited here).
